newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish troops, air force, may hit northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkish troops, air force, may hit northern Iraq.

text.p: Turkish troops, backed by air power, could attack Kurdish separatist rebels at any time, a high-ranking military official said on Thursday.

"There is the possibility of a sudden air-backed assault into northern Iraq. We are thinking of hitting the enemy (Kurdistan Workers Party rebels) all of a sudden without giving it the chance of protection," the military official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters by telephone.

Witnesses said heavy military preparations were in progress near Turkey's volatile border with Iraq. The activity was noted after Turkey's announcement that it was preparing to set up a security cordon inside northern Iraq to halt PKK infiltration.
"We know that two thirds of PKK power and its training centres are established in northern Iraq," the army official said.
Turkey sent 35,000 troops 40 km (25 miles) into northern Iraq to hit PKK positions in March 1995. They withdrew six weeks later.
